turns.content: The RV periodogram has peaks at 71.1, 56.2, and 18.7 days, while H-alpha and Ca II indicators peak at 28.1 days. Describe the observed harmonic relationships without inferring causation.
State the strongest relationship warranted between the activity indicators and RV signals, and whether the available periodograms alone identify activity-to-RV causation.
Given v sin(i)=0.9 km/s and a rotation-axis inclination of 90 degrees, determine the star's equatorial rotation speed.
Using a solar radius and P_rot=2 pi R/v, estimate the stellar rotation period in days.
Compare the RV and activity periods with the rotation estimate. Classify likely rotational or activity harmonics and identify the leading planetary candidate, noting the missing confirmation tests.
State the best-supported planetary period and calibrate the remaining uncertainty in its origin.
Explain briefly why the equatorial speed used in the rotation calculation equals 0.9 km/s.
Identify the signal most likely due to the planet and specify observations that would confirm or refute that interpretation.
Check whether an activity indicator shares the proposed planetary period, and name the most direct coherence or transit-ephemeris test still needed.
Summarize the activity-RV relationship, causal-identification limit, rotation estimate, uncertainty, and signal-origin conclusion.
